tiles.name: x10
tiles.subtitle: 14 MHz
tiles.result: x10 (20 dB) into a high impedance, x5 into 50 ohm, -3 dB near 14 MHz; clips at about +-4 V

tiles.name: x100
tiles.subtitle: 1.4MHz
tiles.result: x100 (40 dB) into a high impedance, -3 dB near 1.4 MHz; keep the input under 40 mV peak

tiles.name: LNA
tiles.subtitle: 30 MHz
tiles.result: x100 (40 dB) from 50 ohm, flat 1-30 MHz, about 3 dB noise figure from 50 ohm; keep the input under 30 mV peak

tiles.name: noise
tiles.subtitle: x100
tiles.result: the source resistor's Johnson noise x100: about 1.3 mV rms from 10 k, 0.4 mV from 1 k, 0.16 mV (the amplifier itself) shorted

tiles.name: 1-bit ADC
tiles.result: a one-bit stream on Pmod 2 whose density follows IN; the FPGA closes the loop through Pmod 1 (the handbook's gateware)

tiles.name: heat
tiles.result: 0.83 W into the board when Pmod 3 is high (the FET's drain), 10 mV/K + 500 mV on OUT

tiles.name: ultrasound
tiles.result: a 40 kHz burst from Pmod 5/6 leaves the TX transducer; its echo arrives x100 on RX OUT (hold a reflector over the board)

tiles.name: power
tiles.subtitle: USB-C 5 V in: +5, -5, +3.3 out
tiles.result: +5 V from the USB-C (up to 1.5 A), -5 V at 40 mA, +3.3 V at 300 mA; the green LED says 5 V is in, the red one that -5 V is up

back_text: AMOD-A: active blocks on USB-C power.  Each tile
has a slide switch (up: on) and SMA jacks: cable
DAC OUT to IN, OUT to ADC IN.  The Pmod plug (left)
takes the FPGA's lines; the handbook has the rest.
